comments.note: The resolveProjectStore() catch block in gui/api.ts (line ~194) swallows all errors including LedgerStore constructor failures (e.g. planFolderBasename pattern mismatch) and returns NOT_FOUND. This makes debugging difficult when .meta.json has a plan_path that fails internal validation — the error message from the constructor is lost. A debug-level stderr log of the caught error inside the catch block would help operators diagnose corrupt .meta.json entries without leaking path information to API clients.

The writeMetaJson() helper in run-log-server.test.ts uses plan_path: '/fake/{repo}/{slug}/plan.md' (no YYYY-MM-DD prefix) which would break if the handler ever calls resolveProjectStore(). The api-run-metadata.test.ts tests discovered this constraint the hard way. A shared test-fixture factory that enforces the correct plan_path format would prevent similar issues in future test files.

The namespaced route block for GET /:repo/:slug/run-metadata at rest.length===4 correctly includes 'run-metadata' keyword exclusion guards on rest[2]. However the existing /:slug/run-metadata route at rest.length===3 appears before the /:repo/:slug catch-all, while the catch-all (rest.length===3) already excludes 'run-metadata' from rest[2]. This is correctly ordered and guarded — no change needed, but worth noting the exclusion was already in place before this WP.

comments.note: No Critical or High security findings. All OWASP Top 10 categories reviewed. The new GET /api/projects/:repo/:slug/run-metadata route (server.ts lines 648–672) follows the established defence-in-depth security pattern: (1) SAFE_SLUG_REGEX enforced at routing layer before decodeURIComponent values are used; (2) assertSafeSlug() re-applied inside the handler via resolveProjectStore() — double validation; (3) resolveRepoName() acts as project-existence gate requiring a valid .meta.json before any handler dispatch; (4) A03/path-traversal: regex /^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]*$/ structurally excludes '.', '/', '%', and all traversal characters — URL-encoded variants decoded first then rejected; (5) A05: CORS restricted to localhost:port, security headers (X-Content-Type-Options, X-Frame-Options, CSP, Referrer-Policy) present on all responses; (6) A01: route is read-only GET, no privilege escalation surface; (7) A10/SSRF: no outbound requests, file I/O bounded to validated path segments.

Info/Low — A09 (Security Logging): resolveRepoName() at server.ts line 322 writes the full metaPath to process.stderr when .meta.json is malformed (e.g., '[server] Warning: malformed .meta.json at /ledger/root/repo/slug/.meta.json'). This exposes internal ledger directory structure in server logs. This is a pre-existing pattern shared by all namespaced routes (not introduced by this WP), and acceptable for a local developer tool. No remediation required for this WP; operators should treat server logs as privileged if the ledger root contains sensitive path components.
